text:
alina: Heads-up — mkdocs build failing on main after yesterday's doc churn. CI shows a bunch of duplicate anchor warnings and then it crashes on the table-of-contents step. full log: `WARNING -  Duplicate ID 'deployment-options' found, used 'deployment-options-1'` then `ERROR -  TOC generation failed`. Anyone seen this?

sam: Repro steps? I can try locally. Which doc changed?

alina: PR is https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482 — I moved the private deployment content into a new page and split a few headings. Locally run: `pipx run mkdocs build` or `mkdocs build -v` shows the same warnings.

docs-bot: CI: build/docs failed for commit a7f4d2c — https://ci.redwood.dev/build/7821 (logs attached) :x: 

mike: Likely a heading collision. MkDocs autogenerates anchors from headings; if two headings slugify to the same anchor you get those '-1' suffices and TOC can blow up if frontmatter or nav expects a specific id. Did we have special unicode chars in headings? e.g. en-dash or emoji?

alina: Yup one heading had an em-dash and another had a hyphen, both ended up generating the same slug. Also one heading had an inline code span which changed the slug in unpredictable ways.

harper: Quick fix: add explicit IDs to the Markdown headings where you see collisions, e.g. `## Private deployment — Dedicated pools {#private-dedicated}`. That's supported by Markdown (and Material for MkDocs). Then update any internal links to the explicit IDs.

sam: Nice. Will that work for Docusaurus too? We have a couple of pages that get built by different toolchains in the past.

mike: Docusaurus supports the `{#id}` syntax too in MDX, but the slug generation rules differ slightly. For cross-tool compatibility you can also use explicit anchor links where needed: `[see dedicated](#private-dedicated)`. Avoid relying on auto-slugs for stable links.

alina: I'm patching the PR: renaming two headings and adding explicit IDs. Also fixing the links in the nav that referenced the old autogenerated anchors. Patch pushed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482/files (commit 3e2b7cd)

ci-bot: Build retriggered for PR #482 (branch: docs/mkdocs-anchor-fix) — https://ci.redwood.dev/build/7823 :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: If CI still fails, can we add a smoke test that runs `mkdocs build` in the pipeline and scans for `Duplicate ID` warnings? We should fail the build on those warnings.

harper: Agreed. You can run `mkdocs build --strict` which turns warnings into errors for some things (but not all plugins). Alternatively grep the output for "Duplicate ID" and fail. I can add a quick job.

mike: Also check table-of-contents entries in the YAML nav: if the nav points to anchors that no longer exist, mkdocs will error. I'd run `rg "#" docs/ | sed -n '1,200p'` to find any manual anchor links.

alina: CI passed on the patched branch :tada: — build/docs succeeded. Deployed preview to staging: https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/482. I updated the PR description to call out the heading ID changes and added a changelog note.

sam: Great. Harper let's follow up with the pipeline change in a separate PR to fail on duplicate anchors. Could add a small util script that runs after `mkdocs build` to scan for `Duplicate ID` patterns.

harper: On it. I’ll open a PR today.

mike: One more thing — there are a few links in older docs that used URL-encoded characters (spaces -> %20) which sometimes result in different anchors after slugification. Might be worth normalizing links to use plain `#id` anchors where possible.

alina: Noted, I'll add a bullet to the docs contributor guide about using explicit `{#id}` for any heading that might be referenced externally.

sam: :thumbsup: Thanks all — closing the loop on this thread.
